在折叠稳定性和活性 imposed by fitness constraints 条件下 进化 的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 主要蛋白酶
item.description: 摘要 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒 2 (严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2) 不断进化和多样化,导致免疫逃避变异体的出现,并强调需要针对保守病毒机制的补充 抗病毒药物 策略。在这种情况下,主要蛋白酶(Mpro)代表了一个潜在的治疗靶点,因为它在病毒复制中发挥着核心作用,并且与人类蛋白酶的相似性较低。然而,Mpro 变异对底物识别和潜在抗性的进化后果尚未得到充分探索。通过对多个 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 Mpro 变体的分析,我们表明,尽管病毒不断多样化,但自 2022 年 Omicron 相关 P132H 谱系出现以来,Mpro 进化 仍然受到显着限制,活性位点和二聚化界面区域的氨基酸替换有限。在最流行的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变体中,Mpro 的整体底物识别在很大程度上得以保留,尽管特定的变体-底物对在每个残基相互作用和氢键模式中表现出一些异质性。整体动力学揭示了某些 Mpro 变体中保守的大规模运动以及次级运动中适度的底物依赖性变化。总体而言,严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 Mpro 进化 受到结构和功能要求的强烈限制,支持该蛋白作为有效的 抗病毒药物 靶标的适用性。研究结果进一步表明,纳入病毒进化动力学可能有助于设计具有改善的长期稳健性的治疗策略。

COVID-19 dashboard
item.description: The WHO COVID-19 dashboard provides global surveillance data on confirmed cases, deaths, hospitalizations, vaccines, variants, and wastewater data. Confirmed cases are defined by positive NAAT tests or clinical/epidemiological criteria with positive antigen tests. Data collection began in December 2019 and continues with weekly reporting since August 2023. WHO compiles data from Member States, with some countries having stopped reporting or changed frequency. Data is subject to verification and may change due to retrospective updates. Weekly reporting mitigates misinterpretation from varying reporting practices. The dashboard includes metadata and definitions to ensure clarity.

item.title: Eating the cost: food prices and the COVID-19 pandemic - Bureau of Labor Statistics (.gov)
item.description: The Bureau of Labor Statistics article published on July 23, 2026, provides a general overview of U.S. economic indicators and BLS resources, rather than reporting on a specific COVID-19 outbreak. It highlights key statistics such as a 4.2% unemployment rate in June 2026, a -0.4% Consumer Price Index for the same month, and other labor market data. The article serves as a guide to accessing BLS information and does not detail any COVID-19-specific events, cases, or response measures. It reflects the ongoing collection and dissemination of economic data by the federal government.

item.title: COVID-19 - Encyclopedia Britannica
item.description: COVID-19, a highly contagious respiratory illness caused by SARS-CoV-2, was first detected in Wuhan, China, in 2019 and quickly spread worldwide, leading to a multiyear pandemic that resulted in millions of deaths. The disease, characterized by symptoms like fever, cough, and shortness of breath, disproportionately affects older adults and those with chronic illnesses. While there is no cure, treatments such as antiviral drugs and monoclonal antibodies are available, and vaccines have been highly effective in reducing severe illness. The pandemic's spread has been driven by variants like Omicron, which are highly infectious and can evade treatments. Survivors of severe cases may experience long-term effects, including neurological issues and prolonged recovery challenges.

item.title: Temporal Changes in Pediatric Influenza Test Positivity Across COVID-19 Public Health Policy Phases: A Five-Year Retrospective Cohort Study - Cureus
item.description: This Cureus study analyzed temporal changes in pediatric influenza test positivity across five years (2018-2023) at a Turkish hospital, examining three COVID-19 policy phases: pre-pandemic, restriction-dominant, and post-restriction periods. Among 18,035 children tested, influenza positivity was highest (28.7%) during strict restrictions but occurred with significantly reduced testing volume. Notably, influenza A positivity increased while influenza B decreased after restrictions eased. The researchers caution that higher test positivity during restrictions doesn't indicate increased population-level circulation, as healthcare utilization changes and testing behavior likely influenced results. The study underscores the complex interplay between public health measures, testing practices, and respiratory virus epidemiology in children.

item.title: COVID-19 cases surge to epidemic levels: CDC - Taipei Times
item.description: The Centers for Disease Control (CDC) in Taiwan reported a surge in COVID-19 cases, reaching epidemic levels with 4,766 new infections, five deaths, and 25 severe cases. The increase marks a 66.5 percent rise compared to the previous week, with severe symptoms predominantly affecting individuals over 65. The CDC highlighted that NB.1.8.1 is the most prevalent SARS-CoV-2 subvariant in Taiwan, accounting for 58.76 percent of global cases. Officials stressed the importance of vaccination, noting that Taiwan’s XBB vaccines reduce acute symptoms and hospitalizations by nearly 50 and 55 percent, respectively. The policy for universal vaccine access will continue until the end of the month, and new vaccines targeting KP.2 are expected in October. Those who developed symptoms after traveling to countries in the western Pacific are advised to seek medical attention and take rapid tests.

item.title: Long COVID symptoms have declined since COVID-19 Omicron but can persist - Labmate Online
item.description: Labmate Online 于 2026 年 7 月 22 日发表的文章讨论了自 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 的 Omicron 变体以来 长新冠 症状的减少,但指出这些症状仍然可能持续存在。该报告本质上是一般性的,没有提供具体的病例数、死亡人数或暴露人数。它还没有提及任何详细的调查、测试或应对措施。重点是感染 Omicron 变种后持续存在的长期症状,强调需要持续监测和了解新冠病毒感染后的情况。该文章没有具体说明受影响的特定地点或人群,也没有提供任何明确的风险评估。内容基于对长新冠症状及其趋势的一般性陈述,没有详细的数据或方法。

item.title: New COVID-19 variant detected in India: Omicron RF.5 is spreading rapidly - Can existing vaccines still protect you? - TheHealthSite
item.description: India is experiencing rapid spread of a new COVID-19 variant, Omicron RF.5, with Andhra Pradesh reporting 12 cases and 4 deaths in three weeks. The state health department has responded by strengthening surveillance and urging preventive measures, particularly for high-risk individuals. While the article confirms the variant's rapid spread, it raises concerns about whether existing vaccines will remain effective against this new subvariant. The situation remains under monitoring with no official statements yet on specific public health interventions or vaccine efficacy data.

item.title: 关于 长新冠 的五个问题 - 英国皇家学会
item.description: The Royal Society has published an article addressing five key questions about Long Covid, a condition affecting approximately 10% of people who contract Covid-19. The condition, characterized by symptoms like chronic fatigue, headache, and cognitive difficulties, can be severely debilitating with unpredictable severity. While SARS-CoV-2 is identified as the trigger, the exact mechanisms causing Long Covid remain unclear. Research suggests potential factors include herpesvirus reactivation, blood vessel malfunction, immune system abnormalities, and autoantibodies that react with nervous system tissues. Despite challenges in definition and diagnosis, ongoing global research has yielded promising findings that may lead to new treatments. The article emphasizes the condition's significant impact on mental health and highlights similarities with ME/CFS, suggesting potential shared therapeutic approaches.

item.title: Is Covid-19 making a comeback? Why India is seeing a spike in cases - The Federal
item.description: India is experiencing localised spikes in COVID-19 cases across several states, including Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, West Bengal, and Bihar. Between June and July 2026, Odisha reported 3 cases, Andhra Pradesh reported 26 cases with 4 deaths, and smaller numbers were noted in other regions. Health authorities characterize these as sporadic, endemic flare-ups rather than a new wave, driven by waning immunity and viral evolution. The four deaths in Andhra Pradesh all involved patients with severe comorbidities. Experts predict ongoing mild, irregular cyclical upticks similar to seasonal flu, with severe risk primarily affecting vulnerable populations. Health departments are maintaining surveillance and urging calm, emphasizing that COVID-19 now behaves like a common respiratory illness for most people.

item.title: Is Kolkata's Covid-19 Rise a Warning Sign? Here's What Doctors Are Saying - Open Magazine
item.description: Kolkata is experiencing a fresh uptick in Covid-19 cases, with hospitals reporting new admissions and doctors noting a rise in respiratory infections. A 10-year-old boy and three other patients have been hospitalized, with two requiring ICU admission due to low oxygen levels before stabilizing. The current increase is driven by sub-variants of the Omicron lineage, which do not appear to cause more severe illness than earlier strains. Symptoms include fever, sore throat, cough, and fatigue, with those underlying conditions potentially experiencing breathlessness. Medical experts urge vigilance, especially for vulnerable groups, and emphasize vaccination as the most effective defense. The healthcare system remains prepared with monitoring and testing capabilities.
